accepted.label: paykit/v1/app-record
accepted.name: mixed-order public key
accepted.why: A is [a]B plus a point of order 8, R = [r]B, S = r + k*a with k a multiple of 8: the cofactorless equation holds; wire 2.1 accepts mixed-order keys

description: One signature per label of wire 2.3, followed by signatures a verifier must reject and unusual ones it must accept (wire 2.1): Ed25519 (RFC 8032, verified as wire 2.1 spells out: S below L, A and R canonical, neither of small order, cofactorless equation) over lp(label, field1, ..., fieldn). signed_bytes_hex is that exact input. Signed documents put the body last; operations, transition proofs and service transitions put the identity's 32-byte key first. In rejections, lenient_accepts says whether ed25519-dalek's non-strict verify takes the signature, and reason the step of wire 2.1 that refuses it, as the prototype words it.

rejections.label: paykit/v1/app-cert
rejections.name: non-canonical S
rejections.why: the wallet certificate's signature with S + L in place of S

rejections.label: paykit/v1/app-cert
rejections.name: small-order public key
rejections.why: public key and R are the identity point, S is 0: holds for any message

rejections.label: paykit/v1/app-record
rejections.name: another label
rejections.why: the wallet certificate's signature checked as an app record

rejections.label: paykit/v1/app-record
rejections.name: cofactored equation only
rejections.why: the mixed-order key with k = 1 mod 8: [8][S]B = [8]R + [8][k]A holds but [S]B = R + [k]A doesn't; Paykit verifies cofactorless

rejections.label: paykit/v1/app-record
rejections.name: small-order R
rejections.why: R is the point of order 2, A the mixed-order key, k = 4 mod 8 and S = k*a: the cofactorless equation holds, but R is of small order

rejections.label: paykit/v1/app-record
rejections.name: non-canonical R
rejections.why: R is the identity point written as y + p (y = 1), S = k*a with k a multiple of 8: decoded, the equation holds; R isn't canonical (and is of small order)

rejections.label: paykit/v1/app-record
rejections.name: non-canonical public key
rejections.why: A is the point with y = 3 written as y + p: it decodes and isn't of small order, but re-encodes to other bytes

rejections.label: paykit/v1/app-record
rejections.name: small-order public key of order 8
rejections.why: A is a point of order 8 (the identity point case is in the list above): refused before the equation
